document.title: Bug reports: screenshots and simpler consent

children.value: Bug reports: screenshots and simpler consent
Bug reporting now starts with useful context and needs no written description. The tutorial keeps the Report bug and Version history controls visible, but disabled.
The dialog captures the Review window before it opens. It shows the JPEG as a removable preview. A user can replace it by pasting or dropping a PNG, JPEG, or WebP image.
The form has two attachment choices:
The request keeps the existing wire flags and adds one optional field:
Review Desktop captures the window through the host screenshot service.
The canvas limits the longest edge to 1600 pixels and re-encodes at JPEG quality 0.8.
The local API accepts at most 6 MiB of JSON and validates a decoded screenshot limit of 3 MiB.
Submission sends the existing gzipped multipart payload to the bug service.
If the multipart payload is too large, the server drops diff, map, screenshot, then Review source. Metadata records whether the screenshot was sent or truncated.
Capture failure and a 1.5 second timeout are non-blocking. The dialog still opens, and paste or drop remains available.
Report bug and Version history use the same disabled visual state during the tutorial. The controls do not capture, load revisions, emit open telemetry, or open a dialog or menu.

props.title: Why OpenCode needed its own shape

children.value: Why OpenCode needed its own shape

Claude Code, Codex, and Pi are each observed through hooks or an app-server already running in the review's own checkout. OpenCode is different: it is server-first, so Review starts and owns a private
process, and every session it creates belongs to a
— not to the review checkout that made the request.
The first version forked and attached using the review's own checkout directory, which put the fork in the wrong project and the server answered
. The fix, in the last commit, looks the source session up by ID first (scanning every project OpenCode knows about) and then forks, prompts, and attaches inside

messages.label: GET /project, then GET /session/:id in each worktree until one answers
POST /session/:id/fork, scoped to the source session's own directory

children.value: One consequence called out in the PR: an OpenCode question session runs in the
, not the review's pinned checkout — different from the other three harnesses.
The second fix addresses a separate problem:
originally waited on the synchronous message endpoint, so a model turn longer than the request timeout aborted before the assistant replied. It now submits with
once a second (10-minute cap, cancellable), failing fast if the assistant message itself carries an error.
